Gramlot 0.2.8 writes down the naming and proxy conventions, stops teaching remote Source, and adds the JavaScript routes package `@gramlot/gramlot/routes`.

## What changes

- New package `@gramlot/gramlot/routes` (`js/src/routes/`): the JavaScript subset of genro-routes. `RoutingClass.registerRoute` marks a method with a `Signature` of named TYTX-typed parameters; `Router` resolves paths through instance branches, fills leftover path segments into the parameters (format-checked, decoded by TYTX code) and passes extra segments as `_extraPath`; `RouterNode.call(kw)` invokes the handler, with the path winning over `kw`; `nodes()` describes the tree. The package imports nothing from the rest of Gramlot; `js/src/routes/README.md` maps every name to genro-routes.
- GC-225 records the naming and proxy conventions; new names, proxies and JS markers derive from it.
- The public documentation no longer teaches remote Source (`@source`, `source(...)`, `remoteSource`): it arrives together with the `remote` grammar attribute and `@endpoint`. The code and its tests stay; its API comments say it is not yet part of the page-writing API.

## Upgrading from 0.2.7

- No change for pages, hosts or adapters.
- Pages that call `remoteSource` keep working; do not start new ones on it.
